summary: Enable OIDC and SAML sign-in when the browser uses a separate public EnterpriseGlue API origin.
userImpact: Company sign-in, invitation enrollment, and OIDC account linking can start on the configured browser API origin.

instructions: For a split deployment, deploy the updated frontend and backend, then align the browser API origin, saved provider callback, and identity-provider registration before enabling SSO enforcement.

configuration: Set EG_PUBLIC_API_ORIGIN on the backend to permit canonical sign-in callbacks on one additional exact origin.

changes: SSO start and callback redirects are non-cacheable. OpenAPI now documents the existing global and tenant OIDC form-post callbacks.

security: Production callbacks require HTTPS. Canonical paths, tenant bindings, and host-only sign-in and session cookies are retained.
knownLimitations: Split-origin sign-in requires same-site browser API access and a trusted shared XSRF cookie domain when the hostnames differ.
SAML single logout and frontend plugin assets retain their existing routing requirements.
rollback: Restore the previous frontend settings, saved provider callback and identity-provider registration before removing EG_PUBLIC_API_ORIGIN or reverting the backend.
validation: Exercise split-origin browser navigation, OIDC and SAML sign-in, bundle preview, same-origin compatibility, and rejected callback URLs.
Compare registered sign-in routes with generated OpenAPI, including redirect headers and callback parameters.
